new.text: The Hebrew will (ʾabâ) answers what another puts before it: a request, "Please let us pass through your land," and the king of Moab "would not consent" (Judg 11:17); "Let my servants go with your servants in the ships," but "Jehoshaphat was not willing" (1Ki 22:49); after days of pressing, "the man would not spend the night" (Judg 19:10); Absalom "pressed him, but he would not go" (2Sa 13:25); "Joab would not come" (2Sa 14:29). A plan allows for another's will: "Perhaps the woman may not be willing to follow me" (Gen 24:5), with a way out, "if the woman is not willing to follow you, then you will be free from this oath" (Gen 24:8). After defeat, "the Syrians were not willing to save the Ammonites anymore" (1Ch 19:19).
